@@@START_FILE@@@
ServerRoot "/usr/local/apache2"
PidFile "/var/www/httpd.pid"

Listen 80

LoadModule mpm_event_module modules/mod_mpm_event.so
LoadModule authn_core_module modules/mod_authn_core.so
LoadModule authz_host_module modules/mod_authz_host.so
LoadModule authz_user_module modules/mod_authz_user.so
LoadModule authz_core_module modules/mod_authz_core.so
LoadModule authnz_ldap_module modules/mod_authnz_ldap.so
LoadModule ldap_module modules/mod_ldap.so
LoadModule auth_basic_module modules/mod_auth_basic.so
LoadModule reqtimeout_module modules/mod_reqtimeout.so
LoadModule filter_module modules/mod_filter.so
LoadModule mime_module modules/mod_mime.so
LoadModule log_config_module modules/mod_log_config.so
LoadModule env_module modules/mod_env.so
LoadModule headers_module modules/mod_headers.so
LoadModule setenvif_module modules/mod_setenvif.so
LoadModule unixd_module modules/mod_unixd.so
LoadModule dir_module modules/mod_dir.so
LoadModule ssl_module modules/mod_ssl.so

ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
FileETag None
TraceEnable Off
Timeout 60
MaxRequestWorkers 100
LimitRequestFields 100
LimitRequestFieldSize 8190
LimitRequestBody 102400
RequestReadTimeout header=20-40,MinRate=500 body=20,MinRate=500

<IfModule unixd_module>
    User www-data
    Group www-data
</IfModule>

DocumentRoot "/var/www/"

<Directory />
    Options None
    AllowOverride None
    Require all denied
</Directory>

<Directory "/var/www/">
    Options None
    AllowOverride None
    AuthType Basic
    AuthName "LDAP Authentication"
    AuthBasicProvider ldap
    AuthLDAPURL "ldap://ldap.example.com:389/dc=example,dc=com?uid?sub?(objectClass=*)"
    AuthLDAPBindDN "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com"
    AuthLDAPBindPassword "secret"
    Require valid-user
    LimitRequestBody 102400
</Directory>

<Files ".ht*">
    Require all denied
</Files>

ErrorLog /proc/self/fd/2
LogLevel warn

<IfModule log_config_module>
    LogFormat "%h %l %u %t \"%r\" %>s %b \"%{Referer}i\" \"%{User-Agent}i\"" combined
    LogFormat "%h %l %u %t \"%r\" %>s %b" common
    CustomLog /proc/self/fd/1 combined
</IfModule>

<IfModule headers_module>
    Header set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
    Header set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"
    Header set X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block"
    Header set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    Header set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self';"
    Header set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    Header unset Server
    Header unset X-Powered-By
    RequestHeader unset Proxy early
</IfModule>

<IfModule mime_module>
    TypesConfig conf/mime.types
    AddType application/x-compress .Z
    AddType application/x-gzip .gz .tgz
    AddDefaultCharset UTF-8
</IfModule>

Listen 443
<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName example.com
    DocumentRoot "/var/www"
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /path/to/cert.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/key.pem
    SSLProtocol all -SSLv3 -TLSv1 -TLSv1.1
    SSLCipherSuite ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
    SSLHonorCipherOrder on
    SSLCompression off
    SSLSessionTickets off
    SSLUseStapling on
    SSLStaplingCache "shmcb:logs/stapling-cache(150000)"
</VirtualHost>
@@@END_FILE@@@

<IfModule mime_module>

    AddType application/x-compress .Z
    AddType application/x-gzip .gz .tgz
</IfModule>

    Listen 443 https

    <VirtualHost *:443>

        SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/key.pem

    </VirtualHost>
</IfModule>

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 Tomcat AJP Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml

        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']

                   address="127.0.0.1"
                   port="8009"
                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add required secret to prevent CVE-2020-1938 if Tomcat9 is installed
    lineinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" secretRequired="true" secret="YOUR_AJP_SECRET" />'
      backrefs: yes
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Restart Tomcat9 service to apply changes
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists and (tomcat_secret_added.changed or tomcat_ajp_blocked.changed)
  - name: Block AJP port 8009 if Tomcat9 is installed
    ufw:
      rule: deny
      port: 8009
      proto: tcp
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists
    notify: reload ufw

  handlers:
    - name: reload ufw
      ufw:
        state: reloaded

@@@END_FILE@@@

        state: restarted

*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT DROP [0:0]

# Allow established connections
-A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 8080 -j ACCEPT

# Application Proxy to Internet
-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.50 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT

# Internal to DMZ Services
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

    <VirtualHost *:443>

        SSLEngine on

        SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/key.pem

        SSLCipherSuite HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5:!3DES

    </VirtualHost>

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 Tomcat AJP Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        state: absent

    - name: Add secure AJP Connector configuration
      blockinfile:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        insertbefore: "</Service>"
        block: |
          <Connector protocol="AJP/1.3"
                   address="127.0.0.1"
                   port="8009"
                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add required secret to prevent CVE-2020-1938 if Tomcat9 is installed
    lineinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '    <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" secretRequired="true" secret="YOUR_AJP_SECRET" />'
      backrefs: yes
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Restart Tomcat9 service to apply changes
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists and (tomcat_secret_added.changed or tomcat_ajp_disabled.changed)
  
  - name: Block AJP connector on port 8009 if secret cannot be set
    replace:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3".*'
      replace: '<!-- <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" redirectPort="8443" /> -->'
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists and not tomcat_secret_added.changed

@@@END_FILE@@@

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 vulnerability in Tomcat
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - name: Stop Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat
        state: stopped

    - name: Download Tomcat 9.0.35
      get_url:
        url: https://archive.apache.org/dist/tomcat/tomcat-9/v9.0.35/bin/apache-tomcat-9.0.35.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp/apache-tomcat-9.0.35.tar.gz

    - name: Extract Tomcat 9.0.35
      unarchive:
        src: /tmp/apache-tomcat-9.0.35.tar.gz
        dest: /opt/
        remote_src: yes

    - name: Update symbolic link
      file:
        src: /opt/apache-tomcat-9.0.35
        dest: /opt/tomcat
        state: link

    - name: Start Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat
        state: started
@@@END_FILE@@@

---
- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 by disabling AJP connector
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure Tomcat server.xml is backed up
      copy:
        src: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        dest: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml.bak
        owner: root
        group: root

        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        state: absent
      notify: restart tomcat

  handlers:
    - name: restart tomcat
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

1. Users with "Owner" or "Admin" level have full control over all areas (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Infrastruktur, Netzwerk, Server, Reporting, Finanzen, Metriken):
   - bot001, bot002, bot003, bot004, bot005, bot006, bot007 (assuming these are bots or system accounts)

2. Users with "Maintainer" level have full control over their respective areas and can contribute to other areas as needed:
   - All users with names starting with "dev" (e.g., dev006, dev007, dev008, dev009, dev010) have Maintainer access for Webentwicklung and Integration, and varying levels of access to other areas based on their specific roles.
   - Users with names starting with "qa" (e.g., qa001, qa002, qa003, qa004, qa005) have Maintainer access for all areas and can perform quality assurance tasks.

3. Users with "Reporter" level contribute to the Integration area and have read-only access to other areas:
   - All users with names starting with "dev" that also have a number (e.g., dev011, dev012, dev013, dev014, dev015, dev016, dev017) have Reporter access for Integration and varying levels of read-only access to other areas based on their specific roles.

4. Users with "Guest" level have limited access to all areas:
   - ext001 has Guest access for all areas except Webentwicklung, where they have Maintainer access.
   - ext002 has Maintainer access for Webentwicklung and Guest access for all other areas.

5. Users with "Owner" or "Admin" level in Appentwicklung also have Guest access to Infrastruktur:
   - All bots/system accounts (bot001, bot002, bot003, bot004, bot005, bot006, bot007) have Guest access to Infrastruktur.

6. Users with "Maintainer" level in Appentwicklung have Guest access to Infrastruktur:
   - All users with names starting with "dev" (e.g., dev001, dev002, dev003) have Guest access to Infrastruktur.

7. Users with "Owner" or "Admin" level in Webentwicklung also have Guest access to Finanzen:
   - All bots/system accounts (bot001, bot002, bot003, bot004, bot005, bot006, bot007) have Guest access to Finanzen.

        dest: /opt/tomcat

    - name: Start Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat
        state: started

iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50/32 -p all -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443,22,25,53 -j ACCEPT

iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.11/32 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ servers to communicate with internet (except Webservers)
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d any -p all -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j DROP
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.10/32 -d any -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,25,53 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11/32 -d any -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,25,53 -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 172.16.20.100/32 -p all -j ACCEPT

# Block all other traffic
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 Tomcat AJP Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml

                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT DROP [0:0]

# Allow established connections
-A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Internal to Application Proxy
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 3128 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 8080 -j ACCEPT

# Application Proxy to Internet
-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.50 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT

# Internal to DMZ Services
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 25 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 587 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 993 -j ACCEPT

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 Tomcat AJP Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml

                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value_here"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if log4j-core.jar exists
    stat:
      path: /srv/app/log4j-core*.jar
    register: log4j_core_exists

        service:
          name: your_app_service_name # Replace with the actual service name
          state: restarted
        when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists
    when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists

---
- name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in PostgreSQL 16
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  become_user: postgres
  tasks:
    - name: Check for fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql
      stat:
        path: /usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql
      register: sql_script

    - name: Fail if fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql does not exist
      fail:
        msg: "fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql not found or version not vulnerable"
      when: not sql_script.stat.exists

    - name: Get list of databases
      command: psql -t -c "SELECT datname FROM pg_database;"
      register: dbs

    - set_fact:
        databases: "{{ dbs.stdout_lines | map('trim') | list }}"

    - name: Allow connections to template0
      command: psql -c "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"
      when: "'template0' in databases"

    - name: Run fix script on all databases
      command: psql -d "{{ item }}" -f /usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql
      loop: "{{ databases }}"
      ignore_errors: yes

    - name: Disallow connections to template0
      command: psql -c "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;"
      when: "'template0' in databases"

# Allow internal clients to access internet via application proxy
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50/32 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50/32 -p all -j ACCEPT

# Allow internal clients to access DMZ services directly
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443,22,25,53 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p all -j ACCEPT

# Allow management network to manage servers via RDP and SSH
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.10/32 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.11/32 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ servers to communicate with internet (except Webservers)
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d any -p all -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j DROP
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.10/32 -d any -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,25,53 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11/32 -d any -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,25,53 -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ servers to communicate with Load Balancer VIP
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 172.16.20.100/32 -p all -j ACCEPT

# Block all other traffic
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

      stat:

      register: log4j_core_jar

fields.content:
Based on the provided data, here's a summary of the permissions for each user in the system:

1. Users with "Owner" or "Admin" level have full control over all areas (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Infrastruktur, Netzwerk, Server, Reporting, Finanzen, Metriken) and are marked as Maintainer for all sections. These users include:
   - Users with names like "your_username" or any other username that has the highest permission level.

2. Developers have control over specific areas (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Infrastruktur, Netzwerk, Server) and may also have some permissions in Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken sections. They are marked as Maintainer for their assigned areas and Reporter for Integration. These users include:
   - Users with names like "dev1", "dev2", "dev3", etc., up to "dev10".
   - Users with names like "dev_finanzen1", "dev_finanzen2", "dev_finanzen3", etc., for the Finanzen section.
   - Users with names like "dev_metriken1", "dev_metriken2", "dev_metriken3", etc., for the Metriken section.

3. Testers have control over specific areas (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Infrastruktur, Netzwerk, Server) and may also have some permissions in Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken sections. They are marked as Maintainer for their assigned areas and Reporter for Integration. These users include:
   - Users with names like "qa1", "qa2", "qa3", etc., up to "qa5".

4. External users (ext001) have limited permissions, mainly in Appentwicklung and Webentwicklung sections as Guest, and no control over Infrastruktur, Netzwerk, Server, Reporting, Finanzen, or Metriken.

5. Bot users (bot001, bot002, bot003, bot004, bot005, bot006, bot007) have control over all areas but their exact permissions are not specified in the provided data.

- hosts: all

@@@START_FILE@@@
# Allow established connections
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Default deny-all policy for INPUT chain
iptables -P INPUT DROP

# Allow incoming traffic on eth0 (DMZ Network)
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT # SSH
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT # HTTP
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT # HTTPS
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT # DNS

# Allow incoming traffic on eth1 (Internal Network)
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -m iprange --src-range 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT # RDP
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -m iprange --src-range 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT # SSH

# Allow incoming traffic on eth1 (Management Network)
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -s 10.1.0.0/24 -m iprange --src-range 10.1.0.0-10.1.0.255 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT # RDP
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -s 10.1.0.0/24 -m iprange --src-range 10.1.0.0-10.1.0.255 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT # SSH

# Allow outgoing traffic on eth0 (DMZ Network)
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT # HTTP
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT # HTTPS
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT # DNS

# Allow outgoing traffic on eth1 (Internal Network)
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth1 -m iprange --src-range 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT # HTTP
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth1 -m iprange --src-range 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT # HTTPS

# Allow internal clients to access the application proxy (172.16.20.50)
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to 172.16.20.50:80
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to 172.16.20.50:443

# Block all other incoming traffic on INPUT chain
iptables -P INPUT DROP

# Allow DMZ servers to communicate directly with the internet
iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o wan0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT # HTTP
iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o wan0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT # HTTPS
iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o wan0 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT # DNS

# Block all other traffic on FORWARD chain
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

40: This appears to be a list of abstracts or titles for presentations at a conference on Korean linguistics. The conference covers various topics in phonology, syntax, and sociolinguistics, including:

**Phonology**

* Tone and intonation in Hamkyung Korean
* Korean labial laterality and articulation theory
* Restriction on consonant clusters
* Merger of back vowels in North Korean dialects
* Vowel length distinction in Modern Korean

**Syntax**

* Word order preferences for direct and indirect objects in children learning Korean
* Constituent order in Korean: antisymmetry and mirror theory
* Case alternations in Korean coordination
* Dependent nouns in Korean as grammatical nouns
* Minimalist interpretation of the visibility condition

**Sociolinguistics**

* Intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology: an analysis of ey and eyse in Korean
* Grammaticalization of particles in Korean
* Semantic change in Korean
* Binding relations in Korean
* Center-embedding and garden-path effects in Korean

**Relative Clauses**

* Against gapless relative clause constructions
* Relative clause or noun complement clause: the diagnoses
* Structure of noun-complementation in Korean: a vew typology
* Demonstratives and relative clauses in Korean

**Case Markers**

* Optimality-theoretic account of Korean nominal inflection
* Korean topic marker and activation
* Pragmatic study of particle (i) na in Korean

**Syllable Structure**

* On the status of on-glides in Korean within optimality theory: evidence from child Korean
* Two-root theory of Korean geminate consonants
* Syllable structure of consonant clusters in Korean

This is just a sample of the many topics covered at the conference.

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 Tomcat AJP Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml

                   port="8009"
                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if log4j-core.jar exists
    stat:
      path: /srv/app/log4j-core.jar
    register: log4j_core_exists

  - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) if log4j-core.jar exists and Java version is 8 or lower
    block:
      - name: Set JAVA_HOME to /usr/lib/jvm/java-1.8.0-openjdk-amd64 if Java 8
        command: "export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.8.0-openjdk-amd64"
        when: "'java version \"1.8.0\"' in ansible_distribution_version"

      - name: Remove JndiLookup.class
        command: "zip -q -d /srv/app/log4j-core.jar org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class"
      when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists and "'java version \"1.8.0\"' in ansible_distribution_version"

  - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) if log4j-core.jar exists and Java version is higher than 8
    block:
      - name: Set JAVA_HOME if Java version is higher than 8
        command: "export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/default-java" # Replace with your actual Java installation path if needed
        when: "'java version \"1.8.0\"' not in ansible_distribution_version"

      - name: Set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups to true
        lineinfile:

          line: "log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true"

        when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists and "'java version \"1.8.0\"' not in ansible_distribution_version"

- hosts: databases
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Find PostgreSQL share directory
      shell: "find /usr -name postgresql -type d -path '*/share/*'"
      register: pg_share_dir
      changed_when: false

    - name: Set fact for PostgreSQL share directory
      set_fact:
        pg_share_dir: "{{ pg_share_dir.stdout_lines[0] }}"
      when: pg_share_dir.stdout_lines is defined and pg_share_dir.stdout_lines | length > 0

    - name: Allow connections to template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"
      when: pg_share_dir is defined

    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "{% raw %}\i {{ pg_share_dir }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql{% endraw %}"
      when: pg_share_dir is defined

    - name: Disallow connections to template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;"
      when: pg_share_dir is defined

    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in template1
      postgresql_query:
        db: template1
        query: "{% raw %}\i {{ pg_share_dir }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql{% endraw %}"
      when: pg_share_dir is defined

    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in other databases
      postgresql_query:
        db: "{{ item }}"
        query: "{% raw %}\i {{ pg_share_dir }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql{% endraw %}"
      when: pg_share_dir is defined and item != 'template0' and item != 'template1'
      loop: "{{ query('postgresql_db', 'SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate = false;').stdout_lines }}"

**Conference Details**

* The conference took place over 4 days, from July 8-11, 1998.
* The conference had various sessions, including:

	+ General Sessions (e.g., Phonology, Sociolinguistics, Syntax)

**Session Abstracts**

Here are some of the abstracts from each session:

**Special Session 1: Relative Clauses**

* Against gapless relative clause constructions by Jong-bok Kim
* Relative clause or noun complement clause: The diagnoses by Jong-yul Cha
* The structure of noun-complementation in Korean: A Vew typology by Hyo Sang Lee

**General Session 1: Phonology**

* The correlation between onset types and tone in Chonnam Korean by Mi-ryung Kim and San Duanmu
* Tone and intonation in Hamkyung Korean: A bottom-up approach by Sung-a Kim
* Korean labial laterality and articulation theory by Kyoung-ja Lee and E. Wyn Roberts

**General Session 2: Sociolinguistics**

* The intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology: An analysis of ey and eyse in Korean by Sung-ock Sohn and Susan Strauss
* Two types of noncausative psych-verbs in Korean and argument/adjunct case particles by Sang-geun Lee

**General Session 3: Syntax**

* Word order preferences for direct and indirect objects in children learning Korean by Sookeun Cho et al.
* Constituent order in Korean: Antisymmetry and mirror theory by Kook-hee Gill et al.

**Other Sessions**

There are many more abstracts listed, covering topics such as:

* Case markers
* Syllable structure
* Romanization in computer-mediated communication
* English loan words in Korean
* Corpus-based analysis of English newspapers published in Korea

These abstracts provide a glimpse into the research being presented at the conference on various aspects of Korean linguistics.

    Require all granted

    Require all granted

    </LimitExcept>

    SSLCipherSuite HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5

    SSLCertificateFile /path/to/cert.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/key.pem

        DocumentRoot "/var/www"

        SSLCertificateFile /path/to/cert.pem
        SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/key.pem
        SSLProtocol All -SSLv2 -SSLv3 -TLSv1 -TLSv1.1
        SSLCipherSuite HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5
        SSLHonorCipherOrder on
        Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
    </VirtualHost>
</IfModule>

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 Tomcat AJP Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml

        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml

                   port="8009"
                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add required secret to prevent CVE-2020-1938 if Tomcat9 is installed
    lineinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8080"'
      line: '    <Connector port="8080" protocol="HTTP/1.1"
               connectionTimeout="20000"
               redirectPort="8443"
               secretRequired="true"
               secret="YOUR_VERY_SECRET_PASSWORD_HERE" />'
      insertafter: '^ *<Connector port="8080"'
      state: present
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Restart Tomcat9 service to apply changes
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

@@@END_FILE@@@

- name: Update Tomcat server to fix CVE-2020-1938 vulnerability
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - name: Stop Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat
        state: stopped

    - name: Download Tomcat 9.0.35
      get_url:
        url: https://archive.apache.org/dist/tomcat/tomcat-9/v9.0.35/bin/apache-tomcat-9.0.35.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp/apache-tomcat-9.0.35.tar.gz

    - name: Extract Tomcat 9.0.35
      unarchive:
        src: /tmp/apache-tomcat-9.0.35.tar.gz
        dest: /opt
        remote_src: yes

    - name: Update symbolic link to point to new Tomcat version
      file:
        src: /opt/apache-tomcat-9.0.35
        dest: /opt/tomcat
        state: link

    - name: Start Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat
        state: started
@@@END_FILE@@@

Based on the provided table, here's a summary of the permissions for each user:

1. Users with `Owner` (e.g., `dev001`, `dev002`) have full control over all repositories (`Webentwicklung`, `Appentwicklung`, `Infrastruktur`, etc.). They can make changes, create branches, and perform any action within the repositories.

2. Users with `Maintainer` permissions (e.g., `dev006`, `dev007`, `qa001`, `qa002`, `qa003`, `qa004`, `qa005`) can make changes, create branches, and perform most actions within the repositories. They do not have full control but have significant permissions.

3. Users with `Developer` permissions (e.g., `dev006`, `dev007`, `dev008`, `dev009`, `dev010`, `dev011`, `dev012`, `dev013`, `dev014`, `dev015`, `dev016`, `dev017`) can contribute to the repositories by making changes and creating branches. They do not have full control but can actively develop the codebase.

4. Users with `Reporter` permissions (e.g., `dev011`, `dev012`, `dev013`, `dev014`, `dev015`, `dev016`, `dev017`) can report issues or bugs within the repositories but do not have the ability to make changes or create branches.

5. Users with `Guest` permissions (e.g., `ext001`, `ext002`) can view the repositories but do not have the ability to make changes, create branches, or perform any action that would modify the codebase.

6. Users with `Bot` permissions (e.g., `bot001`, `bot002`, `bot003`, `bot004`, `bot005`, `bot006`, `bot007`) are likely automated tools or scripts that interact with the repositories, but their specific permissions are not specified in this table.

7. Users with `Owner` for a specific repository (e.g., `dev001` for `Webentwicklung`) have full control over that particular repository, while users with `Maintainer`, `Developer`, or `Reporter` for that repository have the corresponding permissions within that repository only.

8. Users with `Owner` for multiple repositories (e.g., `dev001` for `Webentwicklung`, `Appentwicklung`, and `Infrastruktur`) have full control over all those repositories.

iptables -P FORWARD DROP

iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j DROP

iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11 -d 0/0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j DROP

iptables -P INPUT DROP

@@@START_FILE@@@
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT DROP [0:0]

# Allow established and related connections
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Allow traffic from Internal Network to Application Proxy
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -o eth1 -s 172.16.20.50 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j ACCEPT

# Allow Internal Network to access DMZ directly
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -o eth1 -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j ACCEPT

# Prevent DMZ from accessing Internal Network
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j DROP

# Allow Management Network to manage DMZ servers via SSH and RDP
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,3389 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp -m multiport --sports 22,3389 -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ servers to communicate with the Internet
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.10,172.16.20.11,172.16.20.20,172.16.20.30,172.16.20.100,172.16.20.50 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.10,172.16.20.11,172.16.20.20,172.16.20.30,172.16.20.100,172.16.20.50 -j ACCEPT

# Allow Web Servers to communicate only with Load Balancer
-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.10,172.16.20.11 -d 172.16.20.100 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.10,172.16.20.11 -j ACCEPT

COMMIT
@@@END_FILE@@@

Based on the provided data, here's a summary of the permissions for each user in the system:

1. Users with `Owner` (or `Owner-equivalent`) roles have full control over all modules (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Integration, Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken). These users include:
   - All users with "00" at the end of their username (e.g., user001, user002, ...)
   - Users with specific roles like `maintainer` in all modules (bot001, bot002, ...)

2. Testers/QA members have control over all modules but with read-only access (Maintainer role). These users include:
   - All QA users with "00" at the end of their username (e.g., qa001, qa002, ...)

3. Developers have different levels of permissions based on the module they are working on:
   - Webentwicklung and Appentwicklung developers have read-write access to both modules and read-only access to Integration, Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken (Maintainer role). An example is ext001.
   - Developers working on the Integration module have read-write access to Integration and read-only access to other modules (Developer or Reporter roles depending on the specific task). Examples include dev006, dev007, dev008, dev009, dev010.
   - Developers working on Finanzen and Metriken have read-write access to these modules and read-only access to Integration (Developer role). Examples include dev011, dev012, dev013, dev014, dev015, dev016, dev017.

4. Users with `Admin` roles have full control over the Infrastructure module (Infrastruktur) and read-only access to other modules. An example is bot004.

5. Guests like ext002 have read-only access to all modules in Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Integration, Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken.

# Allow established connections
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Allow incoming traffic on eth0 (DMZ Network)

iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT # RDP for Management Network
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # HTTP for Webservers
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # HTTPS for Webservers

# Allow incoming traffic on eth1 (Internal Network)
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # SSH for Management Network
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -p tcp --dport 3389 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # RDP for Management Network

# Allow incoming traffic on wan0 (Internet)
iptables -A INPUT -i wan0 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # SSH
iptables -A INPUT -i wan0 -p tcp --dport 3389 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # RDP

# Allow outgoing traffic from eth1 (Internal Network)
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth1 -p tcp --sport 22 -j ACCEPT # SSH
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth1 -p tcp --dport 3389 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT # RDP

# Allow outgoing traffic from eth0 (DMZ Network)
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p tcp --sport 80 -j ACCEPT # HTTP for Webservers
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT # HTTPS for Webservers

# Allow outgoing traffic from wan0 (Internet)
iptables -A OUTPUT -o wan0 -p tcp --sport 80 -j ACCEPT # HTTP
iptables -A OUTPUT -o wan0 -p tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT # HTTPS

# Allow internal clients to access the application proxy (172.16.20.50)
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i eth1 -p tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to 172.16.20.50:80
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i eth1 -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to 172.16.20.50:443

# Block all other incoming traffic
iptables -A INPUT -j DROP

# Allow internal clients to access DMZ servers directly
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

# Block all other outgoing traffic
iptables -A OUTPUT -j DROP

@@@END_FILE@@@

- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Find PostgreSQL share directory
      shell: "find / -name fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql -print -quit"
      register: script_location
      failed_when: script_location.rc != 0
      changed_when: false

    - name: Allow connections to template0
      become_user: postgres
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"

    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in template0
      become_user: postgres
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "{{ lookup('file', script_location.stdout | trim) }}"

    - name: Disallow connections to template0
      become_user: postgres

fields.content:
Based on the data provided, here is a summary of the permissions for each user in the system:

1. Users with `Owner` (or `Owner-equivalent`) permissions:
   - Usernames starting with 'bot' (e.g., bot001, bot002, ...) have full control over all repositories (Maintainer permission for all repositories). They are likely automated tools or services.
   - Users with the username pattern 'qa[0-9]' (e.g., qa001, qa002, ...) have Maintainer permissions across all repositories. These users might be Quality Assurance (QA) team members who need access to test and maintain the codebase.
   - Users with the username pattern 'dev[0-9]' (e.g., dev001, dev002, ...) have Maintainer permissions for specific repositories like Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Integration, Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken. These users are likely developers responsible for those specific projects.
   - Users with the username pattern '[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,32}' (e.g., johndoe, JaneDoe, ...) have Maintainer permissions across all repositories if they have an 'owner-equivalent' role, or Maintainer permissions for specific repositories based on their responsibilities within the organization.

2. Users with `Contributor` (or `Reporter`) permissions:
   - Users with the username pattern 'dev[0-9]{2}' (e.g., dev06, dev07, ...) have Developer permissions for specific repositories like Webentwicklung and Integration. They can contribute to the codebase but do not have full control over it.
   - Users with the username pattern 'fin[0-9]{2}' (e.g., fin011, fin012, ...) have Developer permissions for Finanzen and Metriken repositories and Reporter permissions for Integration. They can contribute to these repositories but their changes will need to be reviewed before being merged.
   - User ext001 has Maintainer permissions for Webentwicklung and Appentwicklung repositories, but only Guest permissions for the other repositories. This user might be an external contributor or collaborator who needs access to specific parts of the codebase.
   - User ext002 has Guest permissions across all repositories. This user might be an external reviewer or auditor who needs read-only access to the entire codebase.

# Allow all incoming establishment and related packets

iptables -A INPUT -s 0/0 -d 172.16.20.30 -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT

# Allow incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic from anywhere on port 80 to the DMZ Webservers
iptables -A INPUT -s 0/0 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 0/0 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Allow incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic from the Load Balancer on port 80 to the DMZ Webservers
iptables -A INPUT -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Allow incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic from anywhere on port 443 to the DMZ Webservers
iptables -A INPUT -s 0/0 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 0/0 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Allow incoming RDP traffic from the Management Network on port 3389 to the Internal Network
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT

# Allow incoming SSH traffic from the Management Network on port 22 to the Internal Network
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

# Allow all outgoing packets from anywhere
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth1 -j ACCEPT

# Allow internal clients to access the internet via the Application Proxy
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Allow internal clients to access services in the DMZ directly
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Allow the DMZ to access the internet directly
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 0/0 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 0/0 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT

# Default deny-all policy
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

	* Romanization in computer-mediated communication

	* Restriction on consonant clusters
	* Merger of back vowels in north Korean dialects
	* Vowel length distinctiveness in modern Korean (acoustic analysis)
3. **Syntax**:
	* Reanalysis of dependent nouns in Korean as grammatical nouns
	* Minimalist interpretation of the visibility condition
4. **Sociolinguistics**:
	* Intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology: an analysis of ey and eyse in Korean
	* Grammaticalization of particles in Korean
5. **Relative Clauses**:
	* Against gapless relative clause constructions
	* Relative clause or noun complement clause: the diagnoses
6. **Phonology**:
	* Contextual phonetic palatalization of the Korean affricate /c/ in comparison with Russian consonants

The program also includes a general meeting and presentations on topics such as word order preferences for direct and indirect objects in children learning Korean, constituent order in Korean: antisymmetry and mirror theory, and case alternations in Korean coordination.

Overall, this conference appears to cover various aspects of Korean linguistics, including sociolinguistics, phonology, syntax, and relative clauses.

  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Backup server.xml

        dest: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml.bak

                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="SomeRandomString123!"

    - name: Restart Tomcat

        name: tomcat9

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is running
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: started
    ignore_errors: yes
    register: tomcat_running

  - name: Get current Tomcat version
    shell: dpkg -l | grep tomcat9 | awk '{print $3}'
    register: tomcat_version
    when: tomcat_running.is_changed

  - name: Download Tomcat 9.0.56 package (adjust URL if needed)
    get_url:
      url: https://archive.apache.org/dist/tomcat/tomcat-9/v9.0.56/bin/apache-tomcat-9.0.56.tar.gz
      dest: /tmp/apache-tomcat-9.0.56.tar.gz
      checksum: sha512:7c2e7288c7b225c9e879e052e932b0b242b21b69902e22f2c46a4059af064e4b14982c74cee7fe9505ea6969cf5427d78bc98f51b9466b9969e96a9766048216
    when: tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<') or tomcat_version.stdout is undefined # Update version comparison if necessary

  - name: Extract Tomcat package
    unarchive:
      src: /tmp/apache-tomcat-9.0.56.tar.gz
      dest: /opt/
      remote_src: yes
    when: tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<') or tomcat_version.stdout is undefined # Update version comparison if necessary

  - name: Stop existing Tomcat service
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: stopped
    when: tomcat_running.is_changed

  - name: Configure Tomcat - Disable AJP connector (Recommended)
    lineinfile:
      path: /opt/apache-tomcat-9.0.56/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      state: absent
    when: tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<') or tomcat_version.stdout is undefined # Update version comparison if necessary

  - name: Configure Tomcat - Alternatively, restrict AJP connector (Less Secure)
    blockinfile:
      path: /opt/apache-tomcat-9.0.56/conf/server.xml
      block: |
        <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"
                   redirectPort="8443" address="127.0.0.1" />
    when: tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<') and (not disable_ajp | default(false)) or tomcat_version.stdout is undefined # Update version comparison if necessary

  - name: Remove old Tomcat installation (Optional)
    file:
      path: /opt/apache-tomcat-{{ tomcat_version.stdout }}
      state: absent
    when: tomcat_version.stdout is defined and tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<')

  - name: Create symbolic link for new Tomcat

      src: /opt/apache-tomcat-9.0.56
      dest: /opt/tomcat9
      state: link
    when: tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<') or tomcat_version.stdout is undefined # Update version comparison if necessary


  - name: Start Tomcat
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: started
    when: tomcat_running.is_changed or tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.35', '<') or tomcat_version.stdout is undefined # Update version comparison if necessary

---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Check if log4j-core*.jar exists
      find:
        paths: /srv/app/
        patterns: "log4j-core*.jar"
      register: log4j_core_files

    - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) by removing JndiLookup class if log4j-core*.jar found and Java version is 8 or lower
      block:
        - name: Get Java major version
          command: java -version 2>&1 | awk '/version/ {print $3}' | awk -F '"' '{print $2}' | awk -F '.' '{print $1}'
          register: java_version_output
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: java_version_output.rc != 0 and java_version_output.stdout != "11" and java_version_output.stdout != "17" and java_version_output.stdout != "18" and java_version_output.stdout != "19"

        - name: Set Java major version fact
          set_fact:
            java_major_version: "{{ java_version_output.stdout | int }}"

        - name: Remove JndiLookup class if Java 8 or lower
          when: java_major_version <= 8 and log4j_core_files.matched > 0
          command: zip -q -d "{{ item.path }}" org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class
          with_items: "{{ log4j_core_files.files }}"

    - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) by setting log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups to true if Java version is 9 or higher
      block:
        - name: Get Java major version
          command: java -version 2>&1 | awk '/version/ {print $3}' | awk -F '"' '{print $2}' | awk -F '.' '{print $1}'
          register: java_version_output
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: java_version_output.rc != 0 and java_version_output.stdout != "11" and java_version_output.stdout != "17" and java_version_output.stdout != "18" and java_version_output.stdout != "19"

        - name: Set Java major version fact
          set_fact:
            java_major_version: "{{ java_version_output.stdout | int }}"

        - name: Set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups to true in application startup script
          lineinfile:
            path: /srv/app/startup.sh # Replace with the actual startup script
            line: "LOG4J_OPTS=\"-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true\""
            insertafter: EOF
            create: yes
          when: java_major_version >= 9

    - name: Restart application
      service: 
        name: your_application_service # Replace with the actual service name
        state: restarted
      when: log4j_core_files.matched > 0

@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
# Allow established connections
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Default deny-all policy for all chains
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

# Allow internal network to access application proxy
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50/32 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Allow internal network to access DMZ services directly
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.11/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Allow management network to access internal clients via RDP and SSH
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 3389 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 22 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ servers to communicate with internet (subject to rules below)
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 0.0.0.0/0 -p tcp --dport 22 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 0.0.0.0/0 -p tcp --dport 80 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

# Restrict Webservers to communicate with Load Balancer only
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.10/32 -d 172.16.20.100/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11/32 -d 172.16.20.100/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Deny all other traffic
iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
iptables -A OUTPUT -j DROP
iptables -A FORWARD -j DROP

table ip filter {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop;
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop
    }

    chain forward {
        type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop

        # Internal to DMZ direct access
        iifname eth1 ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.16.20.0/24 accept

        # Internal to Internet via proxy only
        iifname eth1 ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.16.20.50 tcp dport {80,443} accept

        # Management to DMZ for administration
        iifname eth1 ip saddr 10.1.0.0/24 ip daddr 172.16.20.0/24 tcp dport {22,3389} accept

        # DMZ servers to Internet (except webservers)
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.20 oifname wan0 accept
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.30 oifname wan0 accept
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.50 oifname wan0 accept

        # Load Balancer to Web Servers
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.100 ip daddr {172.16.20.10,172.16.20.11} tcp dport 80 accept

        # Internet to Load Balancer VIP
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.100 tcp dport 80 accept

        # Internet to Mail Server
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.20 tcp dport {25,465,587} accept

        # Internet to DNS Server
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.30 tcp dport 53 accept
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.30 udp dport 53 accept
    }

    chain output {
        type filter hook output priority 0; policy drop;
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop
    }
}

**Abstracts are organized by day and session**

The conference runs from July 7-10, with each day featuring multiple sessions on various topics in linguistics.

**Session 1: Phonetics and Phonology (July 7)**

* This session covers topics such as consonant clusters, vowel length, and the merger of back vowels in North Korean dialects.
* Presenters include researchers from universities in Korea, the US, and Japan.

**Session 2: Syntax (July 7)**

* Topics covered include word order preferences for direct and indirect objects in children learning Korean, constituent order in Korean, and case alternations in Korean coordination.
* Researchers from universities in Korea and the US present their findings.

**Session 3: Sociolinguistics (July 7)**

* This session explores topics such as English loanwords in Korean, corpus-based analysis of English newspapers published in Korea, and Korean romanization in computer-mediated communication.
* Presenters come from universities in Korea, the US, and Japan.

**Session 4: Phonology (July 8)**

* Researchers discuss topics like restriction on consonant clusters, vowel length, and the syllable structure of consonant clusters in Korean.
* Presenters include researchers from universities in Korea, the US, and Japan.

**Session 5: Syntax (July 8)**

* Topics covered include a reanalysis of dependent nouns in Korean as grammatical nouns, minimalist interpretation of the visibility condition, and constituent order in Korean.
* Researchers from universities in Korea and the US present their findings.

**Session 6: Sociolinguistics (July 8)**

* This session explores topics such as the intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology, grammaticalization of particles in Korean, and a study on semantic change in Korean.
* Presenters come from universities in Korea, the US, and Japan.

**Session 7: Phonology (July 9)**

* Researchers discuss topics like restriction on consonant clusters, vowel length, and synchronic umlaut and palatalization in Korean.
* Presenters include researchers from universities in Korea, the US, and Japan.

* Topics covered include some notes on binding relations in Korean, grammaticalization of Korean agent-oriented modality, and a study on center-embedding in Korean.
* Researchers from universities in Korea and the US present their findings.

**Other sessions**

40:  Here is a summary of the schedule for the conference:

Day 1 (July 8, 1998):
- Session 1: Syntax (Classroom) - Topics include: a reanalysis of dependent nouns in Korean as grammatical nouns, minimalist interpretation of the visibility condition, and a study on the semantic change in Korean.
- Lunch Break (12:15 - 1:30)
- Session 2: Case Markers (Lunch Session) - Topics include: an optimality-theoretic account of Korean nominal inflection, the korean topic marker and activation, a pragmatic study of particle (i) na in Korean, and two types of noncausative psych-verbs in Korean and argument/adjunct case particles.
- Session 3: Phonology (Conference Room) - Topics include: the intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology in Korean, restriction on consonant clusters, the merger of back vowels in north korean dialects, is vowel length distinctive in modern Korean?, an alternative view on so-called suffixal harmony in Korean, and synchronic umlaut and palatalization in Korean.
- Session 4: Sociolinguistics (Classroom) - Topics include: word order preferences for direct and indirect objects in children learning Korean, constituent order in Korean: antisymmetry and mirror theory, case alternations in Korean coordination, some notes on binding relations in Korean, grammaticalization of korean agent-oriented modality, yo1/yo2 selceng-oy sahoy-enehak - ceck pwunsek, does center-embedding lead to garden-path?, and notes on the binding relations in Korean.

Day 2 (July 9, 1998):
- Session 5: Relative Clauses (Auditorium) - Topics include: against gapless relative clause constructions, relative clause or noun complement clause: the diagnoses, the structure of noun-complementation in Korean: a view typology, demonstratives and relative clauses in Korean, and the contextual phonetic palatalization of the korean affricate /c/ in comparison with the russian consonants.
- Lunch Break (12:30 - 2:30)
- Session 6: Phonology (Conference Room) - Topics include: optimality-theoretic approach to tensification in Korean, synchronic umlaut and palatalization in Korean, cerebral lateralization and korean, japanese, and chinese orthographies: the critical factors for lateralization in recognizing the orthographies.
- General Meeting (Ickl General Meeting) (Auditorium) - Topics include: special II: relative clauses.

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 AJP Vulnerability in Tomcat
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:

        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']

                   port="8009"
                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="random_secret_value_here"
                   allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

- hosts: all

  - name: Check if log4j-core.jar exists
    stat:
      path: /srv/app/log4j-core*.jar
    register: log4j_core_jar

    command: systemctl restart app
    when: log4j_core_jar.stat.exists

  hosts: all
  gather_facts: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Install required packages for OpenSSL patching
      apt:
        name: libssl1.1
        state: present

    - name: Download the patch file
      get_url:
        url: "https://example.com/path/to/openssl-cve2021-44228-patch.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/openssl-cve2021-44228-patch.tar.gz
      become: yes

    - name: Extract the patch file
      tar:
        src: /tmp/openssl-cve2021-44228-patch.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp/openssl-cve2021-44228-patch
      become: yes

        chdir: /usr/lib/ssl/misc
      become: yes

    - name: Restart the application service

      service:

        enabled: no
      when: ansible_os_family == 'RedHat'

    - name: Start the application service after patching (CentOS/RHEL)
      command: systemctl start myapp
      args:
        creates: /var/run/myapp.service
      become: yes
      when: ansible_os_family == 'RedHat'

iptables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j DROP

iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11 -d 0/0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11 -d 0/0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP

iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11 -d 172.16.20.100 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

# Block all other traffic

iptables -A OUTPUT -j DROP
iptables -A FORWARD -j DROP

Based on the data provided, here is a summary of the permissions for each user in the system:

1. The users with the 'Owner' role (represented by the usernames starting with 'bot') have full control over all the projects (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Integration, Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken).

2. The users with the 'Maintainer' role (represented by the usernames not starting with 'bot') are responsible for maintaining specific projects. For example:
   - Users with 'Maintainer' role in Webentwicklung also have 'Maintainer' role in Integration. This indicates that these users work on both Webentwicklung and Integration projects.
   - Users with 'Maintainer' role in Finanzen also have 'Reporter' role in Integration. This suggests that these users contribute to the Integration project by reporting their findings related to Finanzen.

3. The Quality Assurance (QA) team members (represented by usernames starting with 'qa') have 'Maintainer' role for all projects, which means they are responsible for testing and ensuring the quality of the work done on each project.

4. Users with the username 'ext001' and 'ext002' have limited access to all projects as Guests or Maintainers, depending on the project. This indicates that these users may not be directly involved in the development process but might need occasional access for review purposes.

5. The user 'ext001' has a special case where they are a Maintainer for both Webentwicklung and Appentwicklung but only have Guest access to other projects. This suggests that this user is primarily responsible for these two projects but may occasionally require access to the others for review or collaboration purposes.

6. The users with the role 'Developer' (represented by usernames like dev001, dev002, etc.) are working on specific projects within Integration, such as Finanzen and Metriken. However, their roles were not explicitly defined in the provided data.

7. Users with the role 'Reporter' (represented by usernames like rep001, rep002, etc.) contribute to the Integration project by reporting their findings related to Finanzen. Their exact roles within other projects were not specified in the provided data.

40: This appears to be the program for a conference on Korean linguistics, with talks and presentations organized into various sessions. Here's a breakdown of the content:

**Sessions**

1. **Relative Clauses** (July 9, 10:30-12:45)
	* Against gapless relative clause constructions
	* Relative clause or noun complement clause: the diagnoses
	* The structure of noun-complementation in Korean: a vew typology
	* Demonstratives and relative clauses in Korean
2. **Syllable** (July 8, 10:30-12:45)
	* On the status of on-glides in Korean within optimality theory: evidence from child Korean
	* Two-root theory of Korean geminate consonants
	* The syllable structure of consonant clusters in Korean
3. **Phonology** (July 8, 14:00-16:15)
	* The correlation between onset types and tone in Chonnam Korean
	* Tone and intonation in Hamkyung Korean: a bottom-up approach
	* Korean labial laterality and articulation theory
4. **Syntax** (July 9, 10:30-12:45)
	* A reanalysis of dependent nouns in Korean as grammatical nouns
	* On what how behaves like and why
	* Minimalist interpretation of the visibility condition
5. **Sociolinguistics** (July 8, 14:00-16:15)
	* The intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology: an analysis of ey and eyse in Korean
	* Two types of noncausative psych-verbs in Korean and argument/adjunct case particles
	* The grammaticalization of particles in Korean
6. **Syntax** (July 9, 14:00-16:15)
	* Word order preferences for direct and indirect objects in children learning Korean
	* Constituent order in Korean: antisymmetry and mirror theory
	* Case alternations in Korean coordination
7. **Sociolinguistics** (July 8, 10:30-12:45)
	* Korean Romanization in computer-mediated communication
	* English loan words in Korean
	* Corpus-based analysis of English newspapers published in Korea

**Other Events**

* ICKL general meeting on July 9, 17:00-18:00

   Date: July 8, 1998 (Wednesday) - July 9, 1998 (Thursday)

   Venue: [Not Specified]

   Day 1 (July 8, 1998):

   08:30 - 12:30 | Lunch 12:30 - 13:30 | Afternoon Session 13:30 - 17:30

   Morning Session:

   - A Reanalysis of Dependent Nouns in Korean as Grammatical Nouns (Mi-Jeung Jo)
   - On What HOW Behaves Like and Why (Daeho Chung)
   - Minimalist Interpretation of the Visibility Condition (Kiyong Cho)
   - Word Order Preferences for Direct and Indirect Objects in Children Learning Korean (Sookeun Cho et al.)
   - Constituent Order in Korean: Antisymmetry and Mirror Theory (Kook-Hee Gill et al.)
   - Case Alternations in Korean Coordination (Saeyoun Cho)

   Afternoon Session:

   - The Intersection of Diachronic Syntax and Current Morphology: An Analysis of EY and EYSE in Korean (Sung-Ock Sohn & Susan Strauss)
   - Two Types of Noncausative Psych-Verbs in Korean and Argument / Adjunct Case Particles (Sang-Geun Lee)
   - The Grammaticalization of Particles in Korean (Sung-Ock Sohn)
   - A Study on the Semantic Change in Korean (Seung Myong Lee)
   - [Not Specified] (Hyunsoon Kim)
   - Synchronic Umlaut and Palatalization in Korean (Minsu Shim)
   - Cerebral Lateralization and Korean, Japanese, and Chinese Orthographies: The Critical Factors for Lateralization in Recognizing the Orthographies (Kiseong Park)

   Day 2 (July 9, 1998):

   08:30 - 10:30 | Break 10:30 - 10:45 | Lunch 10:45 - 12:45

   Morning Session:

   - Against Gapless Relative Clause Constructions (Jong-Bok Kim)
   - Relative Clause or Noun Complement Clause: The Diagnoses (Jong-Yul Cha)
   - The Structure of Noun-Complementation in Korean: a View Typology (Hyo Sang Lee)
   - Demonstratives and Relative Clauses in Korean (Hyeson Park)

   Afternoon Session:

   - The Contextual Phonetic Palatalization of the Korean Affricate /c/ in Comparison with Russian Consonants (Hyunsoon Kim)
   - An Optimality-Theoretic Approach to Tensification in Korean (Sechang Lee)
   - Some Notes on Binding Relations in Korean (Kyoun-Kook Kim)
   - Grammaticalization of Korean Agent-Oriented Modality (Sangsuk Oh)
   - Does Center-Embedding Lead to Garden-Path? (Sungku Suh)

   Evening Session:
   18:00 - 20:00 | ICKL General Meeting (July 9, 1998; Thursday)

        iifname eth1 ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.16.20.0/24 accept

        # Internal to Internet via proxy only
        iifname eth1 ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.16.20.50 tcp dport {80, 443} accept
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.50 oifname wan0 accept

        # Management access to servers
        iifname eth1 ip saddr 10.1.0.0/24 ip daddr 172.16.20.0/24 tcp dport {22, 3389} accept

        # DMZ servers to Internet (except webservers)
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.20 oifname wan0 accept
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.30 oifname wan0 accept
        iifname eth0 ip saddr 172.16.20.50 oifname wan0 accept

        # Internet to DMZ services
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.100 tcp dport {80, 443} accept
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.20 tcp dport {25, 587, 993} accept
        iifname wan0 ip daddr 172.16.20.30 {tcp dport 53, udp dport 53} accept
    }

    }
}

---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add comment to disable AJP connector
    lineinfile:
      path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      regexp: '^    <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '    <!-- <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" redirectPort="8443" /> -->'
      state: present
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Restart Tomcat
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists and tomcat_changed.changed

  - name: Block AJP port 8009
    ufw:
      rule: deny
      port: 8009
      proto: tcp
      direction: in
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

        name: tomcat9
        state: started

  tasks:
  - name: Check if log4j-core.jar exists
    stat:
      path: /srv/app/log4j-core.jar
    register: log4j_core_exists

        when:
          - log4j_core_exists.stat.exists == True
          - ansible_virtualization_type == 'docker'

- name: Fix CVE-2021-44228 in /srv/app/ without updating
  hosts: all
  gather_facts: no

  tasks:
    - name: Backup application before patching
      copy:
        src: "/srv/app"
        dest: "/srv/app_backup_{{ ansible_date_time.iso8601 }}"
        backup: yes

    - name: Install required tools for patching
      yum:
        name:
          - pkgconfig
          - openssl-devel
          - libxcrypt-devel
          - elfutils-libelf-devel
          - libcap-devel
          - glib2-devel
          - readline-devel
          - java-1.8.0-openjdk-headless
        state: present

    - name: Patch the application with Rust bindings and OpenSSL fixes provided by https://github.com/phpmyadmin/PMA_WebAssembly/releases/download/v5.0.4_20210812/PMA_5.0.4-20210812-webassembly-fixes-rust.tar.gz
      unarchive:
        src: "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/PMA_WebAssembly/releases/download/v5.0.4_20210812/PMA_5.0.4-20210812-webassembly-fixes-rust.tar.gz"
        dest: "/srv/app/"
        remote_src: yes

    - name: Rename existing application to preserve backup
      file:
        src: "/srv/app"
        dst: "/srv/app_old_{{ ansible_date_time.iso8601 }}"

    - name: Symlink the new application to /srv/app
      file:
        src: "/srv/app/"
        dest: "/srv/app"
        state: link

    - name: Restore original permissions and owner on /srv/app
      file:
        path: "/srv/app"
        recursive: yes
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0755'
@@@END_FILE@@@

---
- name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in PostgreSQL
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  become_user: postgres
  tasks:
    - name: Find fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql script
      find:
        paths: /usr/share/postgresql/
        patterns: "fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql"
        recurse: yes
      register: fix_script

    - name: Fail if fix script not found
      fail:
        msg: "fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql script not found."
      when: fix_script.files | length == 0

    - name: Get PostgreSQL major version
      shell: psql -V | awk '{print $3}' | cut -d. -f1
      register: pg_version

    - name: Set fix script path
      set_fact:
        script_path: "{{ fix_script.files | selectattr('path', 'search', '/usr/share/postgresql/' + pg_version.stdout) | map(attribute='path') | list | first }}"

    - name: Get list of databases
      shell: psql -Atc "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate = false OR datname IN ('template0', 'template1');"
      register: databases

    - name: Fix vulnerability for each database
      block:
        - name: Allow connections on template0
          postgresql_query:
            db: "{{ item }}"
            query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"
          when: item == 'template0'

        - name: Run fix script
          command: psql -d "{{ item }}" -f "{{ script_path }}"
          args:
            warn: no

        - name: Disallow connections on template0
          postgresql_query:
            db: "{{ item }}"
            query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;"
          when: item == 'template0'
      loop: "{{ databases.stdout_lines }}"
@@@END_FILE@@@

Based on the provided table, here is a summary of permissions for each user:

- Users with 'Owner' role (e.g., `dev001`): They have full control over all projects in all categories (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Infrastruktur, Reporting, Finanzen, Metriken).
- Users with 'Maintainer' role (e.g., `qa001`, `ext002`): They can modify and manage the projects within their assigned category (for example, `qa001` has control over Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Infrastruktur, Reporting, Finanzen, Metriken). However, they do not have ownership rights and cannot modify other users' work.
- Users with 'Developer' role (e.g., `dev006`, `dev011`): They can create, read, update, and delete content within their assigned category for a specific project (for example, `dev006` can edit the Webentwicklung or Appentwendlung project but not the Integration project).
- Users with 'Reporter' role (e.g., `dev011`, `dev014`): They can only view and report issues for specific projects within their assigned category (for example, they can check for bugs in Finanzen or Metriken projects but cannot modify the code).
- Users with 'Guest' role (e.g., `ext001`): They have limited access to the system and can only view the content within their assigned category (for example, extending functionality or providing feedback for Appentwicklung and Webentwicklung projects).
- Users with 'Bot' role (e.g., `bot001`, `bot007`): They are automated tools that help manage various aspects of the system, such as monitoring, deployments, and reporting.

Overall, this structure allows for a clear separation of responsibilities among team members and ensures that each project is managed effectively while providing adequate access to the necessary resources.

40: This appears to be a conference program for the International Conference on Korean Linguistics (ICKL) held in 1998. It lists various papers and presentations under several categories: Sociolinguistics, Phonology, and Syntax.

Here's a condensed version of the program:

**Day 1: July 6, 1998**

* Plenary Session
* Keynote Speech by Professor John Whitman

**Day 2: July 7, 1998**

* **Sociolinguistics**
	+ Korean Romanization in Computer-Mediated Communication (Esther H. Kim)
	+ English Loan Words in Korean (Jeewon Hahn)
	+ Corpus-Based Analysis of English Newspapers Published in Korea (Kyutae Jung)
* **Phonology**
	+ The Syllable Structure of Consonant Clusters in Korean (Duck-Young Lee)
	+ Two-Root Theory of Korean Geminate Consonants (Eun-Suk Ko)
	+ Restriction on Consonant Clusters (Jongho Jun)

**Day 3: July 8, 1998**

* **Sociolinguistics**
	+ Intersection of Diachronic Syntax and Current Morphology: An Analysis of Ey and Eysye in Korean (Sung-Ock Sohn and Susan Strauss)
	+ Two Types of Noncausative Psych-Verbs in Korean and Argument/Adjunct Case Particles (Sang-Geun Lee)
	+ Grammaticalization of Particles in Korean (Sung-Ock Sohn)
* **Phonology**
	+ Merger of Back Vowels in North Korean Dialects (Soon-Kyong Kahng)
	+ Is Vowel Length Distinctive in Modern Korean? An Acoustic Analysis (Hyunsoon Kim and Jeong-Im Han)

**Day 4: July 9, 1998**

* **Sociolinguistics**
	+ Some Notes on Binding Relations in Korean (Kyoun-Kook Kim)
	+ Grammaticalization of Korean Agent-Oriented Modality (Sangsuk Oh)
* **Phonology**
	+ Contextual Phonetic Palatalization of the Korean Affricate /c/ in Comparison with Russian Consonants (Hyunsoon Kim)
	+ Optimality-Theoretic Approach to Tensification in Korean (Sechang Lee)
	+ Synchronic Umlaut and Palatalization in Korean (Minsu Shim)

**Day 5: July 10, 1998**

* **Syntax**
	+ Word Order Preferences for Direct and Indirect Objects in Children Learning Korean (Sookeun Cho et al.)
	+ Constituent Order in Korean: Antisymmetry and Mirror Theory (Kook-Hee Gill et al.)
	+ Case Alternations in Korean Coordination (Saeyoun Cho)

**General Meeting**

* ICKL General Meeting - Auditorium

Note that this is just a condensed version of the program, and there may be additional papers and presentations not included here.

40:  Here is a summary of the events and presentations from the conference:

Day 1, July 8, 1998:
- Lunch: Kiyong ChoI presented "Minimalist Interpretation of the Visibility Condition"
- Afternoon Session 1 (Auditorium): Sungdai Cho presented "An Optimality-Theoretic Account of Korean Nominal Inflection"
- Afternoon Session 2 (Conference Room): Mi-ryoung Kim and San Duanmu discussed "Tone and Intonation in Hamkyung Korean: A Bottom-up Approach"
- Afternoon Session 3 (Auditorium): Sang-geun Lee presented "Two Types of Noncausative Psych-verbs in Korean and Argument / Adjunct Case Particles"
- Afternoon Session 4 (Conference Room): Kyoung-ja Lee and E. Wyn Roberts discussed "Korean Labial Laterality and Articulation Theory"
- Evening Session (Auditorium): Sung-Ock Sohn presented "The Intersection of Diachronic Syntax and Current Morphology: An Analysis of ey and eyse in Korean"

Day 2, July 9, 1998 (Thursday):
- Morning Session (Auditorium): John Whitman reviewed the paper on Relative Clauses while Byung-soo Park served as a reviewer.
- Afternoon Session 1 (Auditorium): Jong-bok Kim presented "Relative Clause or Noun Complement Clause: The Diagnoses" and Jong-yul Cha discussed "The Structure of Noun-Complementation in Korean: A View Typology"
- Afternoon Session 2 (Conference Room): Hyosang Lee presented "Demonstratives and Relative Clauses in Korean"
- Evening Session (Auditorium): Special II - Relative Clauses, speakers were John Whitman and Byung-soo Park. Jong-bok Kim discussed "Against Gapless Relative Clause Constructions."

The conference ended at 4:45 PM on Day 2.

---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add required secret
    blockinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      block: |
        <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" redirectPort="8443"
           address="127.0.0.1" secretRequired="true" secret="YOUR_SECRET_HERE" />
    notify: restart tomcat
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Restart tomcat
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Workaround - Disable AJP Connector if secret configuration fails
    lineinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      state: present
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '<!--<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
    notify: restart tomcat
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Ensure Tomcat is up to date (within Debian's available packages)
    apt:
      name: tomcat9
      state: latest
      update_cache: yes
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists
  handlers:
  - name: restart tomcat
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted

@@@END_FILE@@@

      </Service>
    </Server>

- name: Mitigate Log4Shell vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Set LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS environment variable
      lineinfile:
        path: /etc/environment
        line: 'LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS=true'
        create: yes

    - name: Remove JndiLookup class
      find:
        paths: /srv/app
        patterns: 'JndiLookup.class'
        recurse: yes
      register: jndi_files

    - name: Delete JndiLookup class files
      file:
        path: "{{ item.path }}"
        state: absent
      with_items: "{{ jndi_files.files }}"

    - name: Add JVM argument to disable JNDI lookups
      lineinfile:
        path: /srv/app/start.sh
        line: 'JAVA_OPTS="$JAVA_OPTS -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true"'
        create: yes

    - name: Restart application
      service:
        name: app
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@
