- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Check if log4j-core.jar exists
      stat:
        path: /srv/app/log4j-core.jar
      register: log4j_core_exists

    - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) if log4j-core.jar exists and Java version is 8 or lower by removing JndiLookup class
      block:
      - name: Check Java version
        shell: java -version 2>&1 | awk '/version/ {print $3}' | tr -d '"'
        register: java_version_output
        when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists

      - name: Extract Java major version
        set_fact:
          java_major_version: "{{ java_version_output.stdout.split('.')[0] | int }}"
        when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists and java_version_output.stdout is defined

      - name: Remove JndiLookup class if Java 8 or lower
        zip:
          path: /srv/app/log4j-core.jar
          delete: org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class
        when:
          - log4j_core_exists.stat.exists
          - java_major_version | int <= 8

    - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) if log4j-core.jar exists and Java version is 9 or higher by setting log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups to true
      block:
      - name: Check Java version
        shell: java -version 2>&1 | awk '/version/ {print $3}' | tr -d '"'
        register: java_version_output
        when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists
      - name: Extract Java major version
        set_fact:
          java_major_version: "{{ java_version_output.stdout.split('.')[0] | int }}"
        when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists and java_version_output.stdout is defined

      - name: Set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups to true in application startup script
        lineinfile:
          path: /srv/app/start.sh # Replace with the actual startup script
          line: 'export LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS=true'
          insertafter: EOF
          create: yes
        when:
          - log4j_core_exists.stat.exists
          - java_major_version | int >= 9

      - name: Restart application to apply changes
        shell: /srv/app/restart.sh # Replace with the actual restart script
        when:
          - log4j_core_exists.stat.exists
          - java_major_version | int >= 9

@@@END_FILE@@@

        paths: /srv/app/

        zip -q -d {{ item.item.path}} org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class

      loop: "{{ jndi_lookup_check.results }}"
      ignore_errors: yes

---
- name: Fix Log4j Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: yes

  tasks:
    - name: Stop Application Service
      service:
        name: app_service
        state: stopped

    - name: Set log4j properties to prevent remote code execution
      lineinfile:
        dest: /etc/log4j.properties
        regexp: '^log4j2.enableRemoteLogging'
        line: 'log4j2.enableRemoteLogging=false'

    - name: Restart Application Service
      service:
        name: app_service
        state: restarted

    - name: Set permissions of /srv/app/ to prevent write access
      file:
        path: /srv/app/
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Remove any existing log4j jar files from the classpath
      find:
        paths: '/srv/app/'
        recurse: yes
        patterns: ['log4j-*.jar']
      register: log4j_jars

    - name: Update /etc/java/option files to prevent loading of vulnerable jars
      template:
        src: templates/java.conf.j2
        dest: /etc/java/java.conf
      notify: restart-java

  handlers:
    - name: restart-java
      service:
        name: java
        state: restarted

- name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in PostgreSQL 16

    - name: Check if fix script exists
      stat:

    - name: Fail if fix script is not found

fields.content:
Based on the provided data, here is a breakdown of the permissions for each user/role in your system:

1. Owners (e.g., dev001, dev002): They have full control over all areas (Web development, App development, Infrastructure, Networking, Server administration, Reporting, Finance, Metrics).

2. Maintainers (e.g., dev003 to dev017, qa001 to qa005): They have full control over their respective areas and can also perform maintenance tasks like fixing bugs and improving functionality in all areas.

3. Reporters (e.g., dev011 to dev013, dev014 to dev017): They can report issues or request changes in all areas but do not have the authority to make those changes themselves. In the case of Integration (Assuming this is a cross-functional area), they are allowed to report issues and request changes there as well due to their development roles in other areas (Finance or Metrics).

4. Testers (e.g., qa001 to qa005): They can perform maintenance tasks like testing new features, fixing bugs, and improving functionality across all areas but do not have full control over the changes they make.

5. Developers working exclusively on App development or Web development (e.g., ext001): They can only work in their designated area(s) and do not have access to infrastructure, networking, server administration, reporting, finance, or metrics.

6. The bot users (bot001 to bot007): Their permissions are not explicitly defined in the provided data. However, assuming these are automated tools or scripts, they should have read/write access to perform their intended functions across all areas as required by their designation (Web development, App development, Integration, Infrastructure, Reporting, Finance, Metrics).

# Allow established and related connections
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Default policy is to drop all traffic
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP

# Block incoming traffic on eth0 (DMZ Network)
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -j DROP

# Allow internal network management traffic
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT

# Allow internal clients to access internet via application proxy
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth1 -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ servers to access internet
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 0/0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 0/0 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT

# Allow Webservers to communicate with Loadbalancer only
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.10 -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.11 -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Block incoming traffic on eth1 (Internal Network)
iptables -A INPUT -i eth1 -j DROP

# Allow internal clients to access DMZ services directly

- name: Fix Tomcat AJP Vulnerability CVE-2020-1938
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']

      blockinfile:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml

          <Connector protocol="AJP/1.3"
                     address="127.0.0.1"
                     port="8009"
                     secretRequired="true"
                     secret="random_secret_value"
                     allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted

-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -j ACCEPT

-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.20 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT

-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.50 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT

-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.10 -j ACCEPT

# Management Network to DMZ Servers for RDP and SSH
-A FORWARD -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT

# Internal Network to Management Network
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 10.1.0.0/24 -j ACCEPT

# Drop any DMZ to Internal Network traffic
-A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/16 -j DROP

   *filter
   :INPUT DROP [0:0]
   :FORWARD DROP [0:0]
   :OUTPUT ACCEPT

   # Internal Network Restrictions
   -A INPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 80 -j REJECT
   -A INPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 -p tcp --dport 443 -j REJECT
   -A INPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
   -A INPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

   # Allow internal clients to access DMZ servers directly
   -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp --dport 80,443,25,53,995,22 -m state --established,related -j ACCEPT
   -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p udp --dport 53,995 -m state --established,related -j ACCEPT

   # DMZ Servers: Communication with Internet and Loadbalancer
   -A FORWARD -d 172.16.20.0/24 ! -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 80,443 -m state --established,related -j ACCEPT
   -A FORWARD -d 172.16.20.0/24 ! -d 172.16.20.100 -p udp --dport 53 -m state --established,related -j ACCEPT
   -A FORWARD -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j CPUMARK --mark 1
   -A FORWARD -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p udp -m udp --dport 53 -j CPUMARK --mark 1
   -A FORWARD -m mark --mark 1 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.16.20.100:80
   -A FORWARD -m mark --mark 1 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.16.20.100:443

   # Allow only Management Network to manage servers via RDP and SSH
   -A FORWARD -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389,22 -m state --established,related -j ACCEPT

   # Default Deny-all policy and establish connections
   -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
   -A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
   @@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- name: Fix Tomcat AJP Vulnerability CVE-2020-1938
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        state: absent

    - name: Add secure AJP Connector with secret and binding to localhost
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service
        add_children:
          - Connector:
              protocol: AJP/1.3
              address: 127.0.0.1
              port: 8009
              redirectPort: 8443
              secretRequired: true
              secret: "{{ lookup('password', '/dev/null chars=ascii_letters,digits length=32') }}"

    - name: Restart Tomcat
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@

---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add required secret to prevent CVE-2020-1938 if Tomcat9 is installed
    lineinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" secretRequired="true" secret="YOUR_SECRET_HERE"/>'
      insertafter: EOF
    notify: restart tomcat9
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Block access to AJP connector (port 8009)
    ufw:
      rule: deny
      port: 8009
      proto: tcp
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  handlers:
    - name: restart tomcat9
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
        enabled: yes


@@@END_FILE@@@

- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Find PostgreSQL share directory
      find:
        paths: /usr/share/
        patterns: postgresql/
      register: postgresql_share_dir

    - name: Set fact for fix script path
      set_fact:
        fix_script_path: "{{ postgresql_share_dir.files[0].path }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql"
      when: postgresql_share_dir.matched > 0

    - name: Allow connections to template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"
      when: postgresql_share_dir.matched > 0

    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "{{ lookup('file', fix_script_path) }}"
      when: postgresql_share_dir.matched > 0

    - name: Disallow connections to template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: template0
        query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;"
      when: postgresql_share_dir.matched > 0
    
    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in template1
      postgresql_query:
        db: template1
        query: "{{ lookup('file', fix_script_path) }}"
      when: postgresql_share_dir.matched > 0

    - name: Get list of databases
      postgresql_query:
        db: postgres
        query: "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate = false;"
      register: database_list
      when: postgresql_share_dir.matched > 0
      failed_when: false

    - name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 in each database

5. The Grammaticalization of Particles in Korean (Sung-Ock Sohn)
6. A Study on the Semantic Change in Korean (Seung Myong Lee)
7. Word Order Preferences for Direct and Indirect Objects in Children Learning Korean (Sookeun Cho et al.)
8. Constituent Order in Korean: Antisymmetry and Mirror Theory (Kook-Hee Gill et al.)
9. Case Alternations in Korean Coordination (Saeyoun Cho)
10. Relative Clauses or Noun Complement Clause: The Diagnoses (Jong-Yul Cha)
11. The Structure of Noun-Complementation in Korean: A View Typology (Hyo Sang Lee)
12. Demonstratives and Relative Clauses in Korean (Hyeson Park)
13. The Contextual Phonetic Palatalization of the Korean Affricate / c / in Comparison with the Russian Consonants (Hyunsoon Kim)
14. Optimality-Theoretic Approach to Tensification in Korean (Sechang Lee)
15. Syncronic Umlaut and Palatalization in Korean (Minsu Shim)
16. Cerebral Lateralization and Korean, Japanese, and Chinese Orthographies: The Critical Factors for Lateralization in Recognizing the Orthographies (Kiseong Park)
17. Some Notes on Binding Relations in Korean (Kyoun-Kook Kim)
18. Grammaticalization of Korean Agent-Oriented Modality, yo1 / yo2 selceng-oy sahoy-enehak - ceck pwunsek (Heesook Kim)
19. Does Center-Embedding Lead to Garden-Path? (Sungku Suh)

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    command: which catalina.sh
    register: tomcat_installed
    failed_when: tomcat_installed.rc != 0 and tomcat_installed.rc != 1
    changed_when: false

  - name: Get current Tomcat version
    shell: catalina.sh version | grep "Server number" | awk '{print $4}'
    register: tomcat_version
    when: tomcat_installed.rc == 0

  - name: Define secret required AJP connector
    lineinfile:
      path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" secretRequired="true" secret="YOUR_AJP_SECRET" />'
      backrefs: yes
    when: tomcat_installed.rc == 0 and tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.30', '<')

  - name: Block  AJP connector
    lineinfile:
      path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" enabled="false" />'
      backrefs: yes
    when: tomcat_installed.rc == 0 and tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.30', '<') and "'secretRequired' not in tomcat_version.stdout"


  - name: Restart Tomcat
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.rc == 0 and tomcat_version.stdout is version('9.0.30', '<')

@@@END_FILE@@@

---
- name: Fix Log4j Vulnerability
  hosts: localhost
  become: true

  tasks:
  - name: Set permissions on /srv/app/
    file:
      path: /srv/app/
      mode: '0755'

  - name: Remove any existing log4j2.xml files
    file:
      state: absent
      path: /srv/app/log4j2.xml

  - name: Replace vulnerable version of Log4j with a non-vulnerable one (if possible)
    copy:
      content: |
        <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
        <Configuration status="WARN">
          <Appenders>
            <ConsoleAppender name="STDOUT" target="SYSTEM_OUT">
              <PatternLayout pattern="%d %p %c - %m%n"/>
            </ConsoleAppender>
          </Appenders>
          <Root level="WARN"><AppenderRef ref="STDOUT"/></Root>
        </Configuration>
      dest: /srv/app/log4j2.xml
      mode: '0644'

  - name: Prevent exploitation of Log4j vulnerability by setting the log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups system property
    lineinfile:
      path: /etc/defaults/java
      regexp: '^JAVA_OPTS='
      line: JAVA_OPTS="-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true"

  - name: Apply changes to all relevant java applications
    shell: |
      for i in $(find /srv/app/*/* -type f); do if [[ $i == *.sh ]]; then sed -i 's/log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=false/log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true/g' $i; fi; done

  - name: Ensure that the log4j2.xml file is not world readable
    file:
      path: /srv/app/log4j2.xml
      mode: '0640'

@@@END_FILE@@@

Date: July 8-9, 1998

Venue: TBD

2. Morphology
	* Dependent Nouns in Korean as Grammatical Nouns
	* Two Types of Noncausative Psych-Verbs in Korean and Argument / Adjunct Case Particles

	* Word Order Preferences for Direct and Indirect Objects in Children Learning Korean
	* Constituent Order in Korean: Antisymmetry and Mirror Theory
	* Case Alternations in Korean Coordination
	* Against Gapless Relative Clause Constructions
	* The Structure of Noun-Complementation in Korean: A View Typology
	* Demonstratives and Relative Clauses in Korean
	* Some Notes on Binding Relations in Korean
	* Grammaticalization of Korean Agent-Oriented Modality
4. Semantics and Pragmatics
	* On What hOw Behaves Like and Why
	* A Study on the Semantic Change in Korean
	* The Correlation between Onset Types and Tone in Chonnam Korean
	* Synchronic Umlaut and Palatalization in Korean

	* Some Notes on Binding Relations in Korean

7. Special Topics
	* Against Gapless Relative Clause Constructions
	* Some Notes on Binding Relations in Korean
	* Heesook Kim's Presentation (TBD)
8. General Meetings
	* July 9, 1998: ICKL General Meeting

## Config Validation
Apache config was invalid:
```
AH00526: Syntax error on line 73 of /usr/local/apache2/conf/httpd.conf:
Unknown Authz provider: valid-user
```
### Default Deny Directive
- Missing Options in root directory block.
### Directory and Location Directives
- Options allows Includes in Directory block for /var/www/website1 
- Options allows Includes in Directory block for /var/www/website2 
- AllowOverride is not set to 'None' in Location block for /restricted
- AllowOverride is not set to 'None' in Location block for /portal
- AllowOverride is not set to 'None' in Location block for /server-status
### Check PIDFile in DocumentRoot
PidFile is located inside the DocumentRoot.
### Required Modules
The following unnecessary auth modules are not enabled:
- Disable authn_core_module
- Disable authz_host_module
- Disable authz_core_module
- Disable auth_basic_module
### Disabled Modules
- Disable status_module
### Apache User Directives
### Directory Options
### Server Status and Info Directives
- The <Location /server-status> block is active and should be commented out.
### Trace Disable Directives
- TraceEnable is not set to 'off'.
- No <LimitExcept\> directive found in a <Directory\> block.
### Security Headers
- Missing or incorrect X-Frame-Options configuration.
- Missing or incorrect Content-Security-Policy configuration.
### SSL Configuration
- SSLCipherSuite should exclude: !low, !dss, !null, !anull, !enull, !3des, !exp, !psk, !medium, !des, !rc4, !dh, !md5

---
- name: Fix Tomcat AJP Vulnerability (CVE-2020-1938)
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Disable AJP Connector in server.xml
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        attribute: port
        value: '-1'

    - name: Add secret required attribute to AJP Connector
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        attribute: secretRequired
        value: 'true'

    - name: Set AJP Connector address to localhost only
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        attribute: address
        value: '127.0.0.1'

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9
    register: tomcat_installed

  - name: Add comment to disable AJP connector (if Tomcat is installed)
    lineinfile:
      path: /usr/share/tomcat9/conf/server.xml
      regexp: '^ *<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"'
      line: '<!-- <Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3" redirectPort="8443" /> -->'
      state: present
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

  - name: Restart Tomcat
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists and tomcat_installed.stat.isdir

@@@END_FILE@@@

   - name: Install OpenJDK and set default JAVA_HOME
     apt: name=openjdk8 state=latest
     command: update-alternatives --config java

   - name: Download Tomcat9 from tomcat.apache.org
     get_url: url=https://mirrors.edge.kernel.org/pub/software/apache/tomcat/tomcat-9/v8.5.67/bin/linux-x64/apt-Getter
     args: creator=wget --quiet --show-progress -P {{ playbook_dir }}/tomcat-installer/

   - name: Create directory for Tomcat installer scripts
     file: path={{ playbook_dir }}/tomcat-installer/ directory='yes' state=directory

   - name: Fix executable rights on downloaded script
     file: path={{ playbook_dir }}/tomcat-installer/apt-Getter perm=0644 state=file

   - name: Make apt-Getter executable
     command: chmod +x {{ playbook_dir }}/tomcat-installer/apt-Getter

   - name: Install Tomcat using installer script
     command: /bin/bash {{ playbook_dir }}/tomcat-installer/apt-Getter --user tomcat --group tomcat >> /dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl restart tomcat9
   @@@END_FILE@@@

---
- name: Mitigate Log4Shell vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Set LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS
      lineinfile:
        path: /etc/environment
        line: 'LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS=true'
        create: yes

    - name: Find log4j jar files
      find:
        paths: /srv/app
        recurse: yes
        patterns: '*log4j-core*.jar'
      register: log4j_files

    - name: Remove JndiLookup class
      shell: zip -q -d {{ item.path }} org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class
      with_items: "{{ log4j_files.files }}"
      ignore_errors: yes
@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Check if log4j-core.jar exists
      stat:
        path: /srv/app/log4j-core*.jar
      register: log4j_core_jar_exists

    - name: Mitigate Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) by setting system property
      lineinfile:
        path: /srv/app/start.sh # Or wherever the startup script is
        line: '-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true'
        insertafter: '^java'
        create: yes
      when: log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.exists and log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.isfile

    - name: Mitigate Log4Shell for older versions (CVE-2021-44228) by removing JndiLookup class
      zip:
        path: /srv/app/log4j-core*.jar
        mode: a
        files: []
      when: log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.exists and log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.isfile
      notify: Restart application


    - name: Find Java process ID
      command: "pgrep -f 'java'"
      register: java_pid
      when: log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.exists and log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.isfile

    - name: Restart Java application
      become: true
      command: "kill -HUP {{ java_pid.stdout }}"
      when: java_pid.stdout != "" and log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.exists and log4j_core_jar_exists.stat.isfile

  handlers:
    - name: Restart application
      become: true
      shell: "/srv/app/restart.sh" # Replace with the actual restart command

@@@END_FILE@@@

  become: true

      register: database_list

        db: postgres
        query: "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"
      when: '"template0" not in database_list.query_result'

    - name: Add template0 to the database list if it was originally disallowed

fields.content:
@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- name: Mitigate CVE-2024-6387 in SSHD
  hosts: all
  become: yes

  tasks:
    - name: Configure SSHD to mitigate CVE-2024-6387
      lineinfile:
        path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        regexp: '^LoginGraceTime'
        line: 'LoginGraceTime 20s'
        state: present
        create: yes

    - name: Ensure SSHD service is running and enabled
      systemd:
        name: sshd
        state: restarted
        enabled: yes
@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
# Allow all incoming traffic on Wan interface (Internet)
iptables -A INPUT ! -s 0/0 -i wan0 --dport 1:1024 -j ACCEPT

# Allow Established connections
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

# DMZ Network Rule
iptables -A FORWARD -d 172.16.20.0/24 -g wan0 -j ACCEPT

# Internal Restriction Rules
iptables -A OUTPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 ! -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80,443 -j DROP
iptables -A OUTPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 ! -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22-1024 -j DROP

# Management Network Allow RDP and SSH to Internet via APP proxy (Only)
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -s 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389 -d 172.16.20.50 -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j DNAT
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -s 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22-1024 -d 172.16.20.50 -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j DNAT

# Allow Management Network Traffic
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.1.0.0/24 -g wan0 -j ACCEPT

# Block Internet Access from Internal
iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d ! 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --syn -j DROP

# Allow Established and Related Connections through Firewall
iptables -A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Set Policy
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP

# Drop All other traffic to Wan interface
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -s 172.16.20.0/24 ! -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --syn -j DROP

@@@END_FILE@@@

40: This appears to be a conference program for the International Conference on Korean Linguistics (ICKL), held in 1998. The program includes a list of presentations, each with its own title and description, grouped into various categories such as phonology, morphology, syntax, and sociolinguistics.

Here is a brief summary of some of the topics presented at the conference:

**Phonology**

* Tone and intonation in Hamgyong Korean: A bottom-up approach
* Restriction on consonant clusters in Korean
* The merger of back vowels in North Korean dialects

**Syntax**

* Against gapless relative clause constructions
* Constituent order in Korean: Antisymmetry and mirror theory
* Case alternations in Korean coordination
* Minimalist interpretation of the visibility condition

**Sociolinguistics**

* Grammaticalization of particles in Korean
* Semantic change in Korean
* The intersection of diachronic syntax and current morphology: An analysis of "ey" and "eyse" in Korean

**Morphology**

* An optimality-theoretic account of Korean nominal inflection
* The structure of noun-complementation in Korean: A typological view

**Linguistic Typology**

* Relative clauses or noun complement clause: Diagnoses
* Demonstratives and relative clauses in Korean

This is just a small selection from the conference program. There are many more presentations listed, covering various topics in linguistics related to the Korean language.

If you're looking for information on specific topics or researchers, I can help you identify the relevant presentation(s). Just let me know!

- name: Fix Tomcat CVE-2020-1938
  hosts: tomcat_servers
  become: yes

        name: tomcat9

- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Check if Tomcat is installed
    stat:

      state: restarted
    when: tomcat_installed.stat.exists

---
- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938 (Ghostcat) in Tomcat9
  hosts: tomcat_servers
  become: yes

  tasks:
    - name: Check if AJP connector is enabled
      command: grep 'Connector port="8009"' /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      register: ajp_enabled
      ignore_errors: yes

    - name: Disable AJP Connector
      replace:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        regexp: '(<Connector\s+protocol="AJP/1.3".*>)'
        replace: '<!-- \1 -->'
      when: ajp_enabled.rc == 0

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      service:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@

- name: Fix CVE-2020-1938
  hosts: your-hostname
  become: yes

  vars:
    tomcat_config_file: "/etc/tomcat9/server.xml"

  tasks:

  - name: Set attribute 'proxyName' to '*' in server.xml

      path: "{{ tomcat_config_file }}"
      regexp: ".*proxyName"
      line: "proxyName=*"

  - name: Ensure proxyPort is at least 8009
    lineinfile:
      path: "{{ tomcat_config_file }}"
      regexp: ".*proxyPort"
      line: "proxyPort=8009"
      state: present

  - name: Set attribute 'acceptCounts' to '*' in server.xml
    lineinfile:
      path: "{{ tomcat_config_file }}"
      regexp: ".*acceptCount"
      line: "acceptCount=*"

  - name: Ensure connectionTimeOut is set to at least 20000
    lineinfile:
      path: "{{ tomcat_config_file }}"
      regexp: ".*connectionTimeout"
      line: "connectionTimeout=20000"
      state: present

  - name: Restart Tomcat service
    service:
      name: tomcat9
      state: restarted

        line: 'JAVA_OPTS="-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true"'
        create: yes

        name: app
        state: restarted

- name: Mitigate CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure mitigation environment variable is set
      lineinfile:
        path: /srv/app/.env
        create: yes
        line: "LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS=true"
    
    - name: Find all jar files in /srv/app
      find:
        paths: /srv/app
        patterns: "*.jar"
      register: jar_files

    - name: Backup original jar files
      copy:
        src: "{{ item.path }}"
        dest: "/srv/app/backup/"
        remote_src: yes
      with_items: "{{ jar_files.files }}"
    
    - name: Run workaround command on jar files
      command: >
        zip -q -d {{ item.path }} org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class
      with_items: "{{ jar_files.files }}"
      become: yes

    - name: Verify mitigation applied to jar files
      shell: "unzip -l {{ item.path }} | grep 'JndiLookup.class'"
      with_items: "{{ jar_files.files }}"
      register: check_mitigation
      failed_when: check_mitigation.rc == 0
      changed_when: false

   - hosts: app_hosts
     become: yes

     tasks:
       - name: Download an exploit mitigation script for CVE-2021-44228
         get:
           dest: /usr/local/bin/java-cve-2021-44228-mitigation.sh
           url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/critical-patch Adams/master/Linux_x64/java-cve-2021-44228-mitigation.sh
         mode: '0755'

       - name: Set environment variable to point to the mitigation script
         ansible.builtin.environment:
           - name: JAVA_OPTS
             value: "-Djava.security.egd=file:///dev/urandom -Xrs -XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:MaxRAMFraction=256m -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:G1NewSizePercent=30 -XX:G1ReservePercent=20 -Xms256m -Xmx512m -Djdk.http.auth.daemon.debug=false -noverify -Djava.awt.headless=true -verbose:class -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/var/log/java_heap_dumps -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true  $JAVA_OPTS"
         when: ansible_os_family == 'RedHat' or ansible_os_family == 'CentOS' or ansible_os_family == 'OracleLinux'

       - name: Apply the exploit mitigation on systemd service file for java
         servicekIT:
           path: /lib/systemd/system/java.service
           template: "j2/java-cve-2021-44228-mitigation-servicefile.j2"
         when: ansible_os_family == 'RedHat' or ansible_os_family == 'CentOS' or ansible_os_family == 'OracleLinux'

       - name: Apply the exploit mitigation on systemv service file for java
        copy:
           dest: /etc/init.d/java
           content: "| sed '/JAVA_OPTS=/{N};s/.*/& "$(sed '0,/$JAVA_OPTS=([^"]*)/"$JAVA_XMX=256m"' -r)"
         when: ansible_os == 'Debian' or ansible_os == 'Ubuntu'

       - name: Restart java service to apply changes
         servicekIT:
           name: java
           state: restarted
         when: ansible_os_family == 'RedHat' or ansible_os_family == 'CentOS' or ansible_os_family == 'OracleLinux' or ansible_os == 'Debian' or ansible_os == 'Ubuntu'
   @@@END_FILE@@@

- name: Fix PostgreSQL CVE-2024-4317 Vulnerability
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Allow connections to template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: postgres
        query: ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;
      become_user: postgres

    - name: Get all database names
      postgresql_query:
        db: postgres
        query: SELECT datname FROM pg_database;
      register: databases
      become_user: postgres

    - name: Apply fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql to all databases
      postgresql_query:
        db: "{{ item.datname }}"
        path_to_script: /usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql
      loop: "{{ databases.query_result }}"
      become_user: postgres

    - name: Disable connections to template0
      postgresql_query:
        db: postgres
        query: ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
      become_user: postgres
@@@END_FILE@@@

fields.content:
This file seems to outline the permissions for various users in a Git repository or similar project management system. Here's a breakdown:

- The accounts with the name starting with "dev" are likely developers with different levels of access. For example, "dev006", "dev0011", etc., all have maintainership over 'Webentwicklung', indicating they can make changes to that branch/project. Additionally, some of these users (like dev006) also have developer-level permissions for 'Integration'.
  - Notice that every developer has read and execute permissions (Maintainer or Guest) for all projects except one (their primary project). This allows them to view and run code in other repositories, but not make changes.

- The accounts with the name starting with "qa" are testers, as indicated by their Maintainer or higher permissions for the 'Integration' project along with permissions for each individual project (Webentwicklung, Appentwicklung, Reporting, Finanzen, and Metriken). This suggests they are responsible for testing changes made by developers in those projects.

- "ext001" is an external contributor, with maintainership over 'Appentwicklung' and 'Webentwicklung'. They have guest permissions for all other projects, meaning they can view the code but not make changes to those repositories.

 - "ext002" has similar permissions as "ext001", but restricted only to 'Webentwicklung' (maintainer) and the rest of the repositories as guest.

- The accounts starting with "bot" are automated bot accounts, likely for CI/CD tools or Git hook scripts used for automation tasks like testing, deployment, etc. They have maintainership over every project (indicating they can make changes on these repositories), a common practice since bots don't need extensive permissions to avoid unintentional errors.

- The users with names "dev#" have additional roles related to project administration ("Infrastruktur") and networking ("Netzwerk") beyond their primary project, potentially indicating that they handle platform setup, server maintenance, or similar tasks.

Finally, all accounts have read permissions for the 'Infrastruktur' and other projects as maintainers or guests, reflecting transparency in the project management and collaboration between team members.

@@@START_FILE@@@
table inet filter {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop;

        ct state established,related accept

        # Allow management network to manage DMZ servers via SSH and RDP
        ip saddr 10.1.0.0/24 ip daddr {172.16.20.10, 172.16.20.11, 172.16.20.20, 172.16.20.30, 172.16.20.50, 172.16.20.100} tcp dport {22, 3389} accept

        # Allow loopback
        iif lo accept
    }

    chain output {
        type filter hook output priority 0; policy drop;

        ct state established,related accept

        # Allow all outbound traffic from the firewall itself if necessary
        # (Assuming no specific services are running on the firewall)
    }

    chain forward {
        type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;

        ct state established,related accept

        # Internal to DMZ
        ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.16.20.0/24 accept
        ip saddr 10.1.0.0/24 ip daddr 172.16.20.0/24 accept

        # Internal to Internet via Application Proxy
        ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr != 172.16.20.50 accept
        ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 oif wan0 ip daddr != 172.16.20.50 drop

        # Allow internal clients to access internet only via application proxy
        meta oif wan0 ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 ip daddr != 172.16.20.50 accept

        # DMZ servers access internet
        ip saddr {172.16.20.20, 172.16.20.30, 172.16.20.100, 172.16.20.50} oif wan0 accept

        # Web servers communicate with load balancer only
        ip saddr {172.16.20.10, 172.16.20.11} ip daddr 172.16.20.100 accept

        # Prevent DMZ from accessing internal networks
        ip saddr 172.16.20.0/24 ip daddr 10.0.0.0/16 drop
        ip saddr 172.16.20.0/24 ip daddr 10.1.0.0/24 drop
    }
}
@@@END_FILE@@@

- name: Mitigate Tomcat AJP Ghostcat vulnerability (CVE-2020-1938)
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure server.xml exists
      stat:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      register: server_xml

    - name: Disable AJP connector
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        state: absent
      when: server_xml.stat.exists

    - name: Add secured AJP connector with requiredSecret
      blockinfile:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        insertbefore: "</Service>"
        marker: "<!-- {mark} ANSIBLE MANAGED AJP CONNECTOR -->"
        block: |
          <Connector protocol="AJP/1.3"
                    address="127.0.0.1"
                    port="8009"
                    redirectPort="8443"
                    secretRequired="true"
                    secret="changeme123456789"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat
      systemd:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
   - hosts: all
     become: yes

     tasks:
       - name: Update apt-get package cache repository
         apt: update_cache=yes

       - name: Install OpenJDK
         apt: name=openjdk-8-jdk state=latest

       - name: Download Apache Tomcat
         get_url: url="http://mirror.centos.org/pub/centos/7/extras/x86_64/Packages/t/tomcat-9*_all.rpm" dest="/tmp/tomcat.rpm"

       - name: Install Apache Tomcat (Debian requires packages to be installed from Debian repositories, but we temporarily use yum-install to handle RPM package)
         yum: pkg="tomcat-9*_all" state=installed mode=0644 src="{{ '/tmp/tomcat.rpm' }}"

       - name: Disable the Tomcat default SSL connector
         lineinfile: dest="/etc/tomcat9/server.xml" regexp='<Connector port="8443" protocol="HTTP/1.1" SSLEngine="on" '\
                    'maxThreads="150" scheme="https" secure="true" keystoreFile="{}/etc/tomcat9/keystore" keystorePass="changeit" keystoreType="JKS"/>' \
                    backup='yes' state=absent

       - name: Replace the Tomcat default HTTP connector
         lineinfile: dest="/etc/tomcat9/server.xml" regexp='<Connector port="8080" protocol="HTTP/1.1" '\
                    'connectionTimeout="20000" redirectPort="8443"'\

  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Check if PostgreSQL is installed

      register: postgresql_installed
      ignore_errors: yes

        msg: "PostgreSQL server is not installed."
      when: postgresql_installed.rc != 0

- name: Mitigate CVE-2024-6387 vulnerability in sshd
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure SSHD configuration directory exists
      file:
        path: /etc/ssh
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

      args:

        insertafter: EOF
      with_items:
        - "LoginGraceTime 30"
        - "MaxAuthTries 3"

    - name: Restart sshd service to apply changes
      service:
        name: sshd
        state: restarted

@@@START_FILE@@@
- name: Fix Apache Tomcat AJP Connector vulnerability CVE-2020-1938
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure AJP Connector is disabled in server.xml
      xml:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        xpath: /Server/Service/Connector[@protocol='AJP/1.3']
        state: absent

    - name: Add secure AJP Connector configuration
      blockinfile:
        path: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
        insertbefore: "</Service>"
        block: |
          <Connector protocol="AJP/1.3"
                   address="127.0.0.1"
                   port="8009"
                   redirectPort="8443"
                   secretRequired="true"
                   secret="changeme123456"/>

    - name: Restart Tomcat service
      systemd:
        name: tomcat9
        state: restarted
@@@END_FILE@@@

      register: result

      shell: psql -d postgres -c "\i /usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql"

      delegate_to: 127.0.0.1
      become_user: postgres

        chdir: /home/postgres/catlogs
        stdin: >-
          ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- name: Fix CVE-2024-4317 on PostgreSQL 16
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  vars:
    sql_script_path: "/usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql"
  tasks:
    - name: Check PostgreSQL version
      command: psql --version
      register: psql_version

    - name: Ensure PostgreSQL version is 16
      fail:
        msg: "PostgreSQL version is not 16."
      when: "'postgres (PostgreSQL) 16' not in psql_version.stdout"

    - name: Check if SQL script exists
      stat:
        path: "{{ sql_script_path }}"
      register: script_stat

    - name: Fail if SQL script does not exist
      fail:
        msg: "SQL script fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql not found."
      when: not script_stat.stat.exists

    - name: Get list of databases
      command: psql -U postgres -d postgres -t -c "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate = false;"
      register: db_list

    - name: Include template0 and template1 in databases
      set_fact:
        all_databases: "{{ db_list.stdout_lines + ['template0', 'template1'] }}"

    - name: Allow connections to template0
      command: psql -U postgres -d template0 -c "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"
      when: "'template0' in all_databases"

    - name: Run fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql on all databases
      command: psql -U postgres -d "{{ item }}" -f "{{ sql_script_path }}"
      loop: "{{ all_databases }}"
      ignore_errors: yes

    - name: Disallow connections to template0
      command: psql -U postgres -d template0 -c "ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;"
      when: "'template0' in all_databases"

*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT DROP [0:0]

# Allow established connections
-A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Internal network to DMZ services
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 25 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 587 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 993 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.30 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.30 -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Internal network to Application Proxy
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 8080 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50 -p tcp --dport 3128 -j ACCEPT

# Management network access to servers
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth1 -s 10.1.0.0/24 -d 172.16.20.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

# DMZ servers to Internet (except web servers)
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.20 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.30 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.50 -o wan0 -j ACCEPT

# Load Balancer to Web Servers
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.10 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i eth0 -s 172.16.20.100 -d 172.16.20.11 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Internet to Load Balancer
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.100 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Internet to Mail Server
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 25 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.20 -p tcp --dport 587 -j ACCEPT

# Internet to DNS Server
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.30 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i wan0 -d 172.16.20.30 -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT

COMMIT

@@@START_FILE@@@
# Default Policy: DROP all traffic
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP

# Allow established connections (no new ones)
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Accept management network IP on RDP and SSH
iptables -I INPUT 1 -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 3389 -j ACCEPT
iptables -I INPUT 2 -d 10.1.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

# Allow DMZ network to access internet (subject to further rules)
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.16.20.0/24 -o wan0 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

# Restrict internal clients to only use application proxy for internet
iptables -I INPUT 3 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.50/32 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -o eth0 -d 172.16.20.50/32 --dport 8080 -j ACCEPT

# Allow internal clients to access DMZ services directly
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.0.0/16 -m iprange --src-range 10.0.0.1-10.255.255.254 -d 172.16.20.10/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 172.16.20.10/32 --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Allow Webservers to communicate with Load Balancer only
iptables -I INPUT 4 -s 172.16.20.10/32 -d 172.16.20.100/32 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -s 172.16.20.10/32 -d 172.16.20.100/32 --dport 80 -j ACCEPT

# Allow web servers to talk to Application Proxy for management and DNS resolution
iptables -I INPUT 5 -s 172.16.20.10-172.16.20.11 -p tcp --syn --dport 22,53,80 -m iprange --src-range 10.0.0.1-10.255.255.254,172.16.20.50/32 -j ACCEPT

# Deny all incoming traffic coming from anywhere other than specified above
iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
@@@END_FILE@@@

@@@START_FILE@@@
---
- name: Fix Tomcat vulnerability CVE-2020-1938
  hosts: tomcat-servers
  become: yes

  tasks:
  - name: Change AJP port to a non-default value
    lineinfile:
      dest: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      regexp: ' AJPort="8009" '
      line: ' AJPort="9009" '

  - name: Limit the ajp protocol using the 'protocol' attribute in server.xml, change from the default of "*", or "HTTP/1.1", to a specific host name like "example.com", or a subnet.
    lineinfile:
      dest: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      regexp: ' protocol="*" '
      line: ' protocol="HTTP/1.1"'

  - name: Set the AJP connector's secret attribute in server.xml, it should be enabled for all ajp connectors. This value needs to be unique for each connector.
    lineinfile:
      dest: /etc/tomcat9/server.xml
      regexp: ' secret=""\s'
      line: '    secret="unique-secret" '

        path: /srv/app/log4j-core.jar

        insertafter: '^<Configuration'
        create: yes
      when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists


    - name: Restart application
      service:
        name: your_application_service
        state: restarted
      when: log4j_core_exists.stat.exists

  hosts: localhost
  become: yes

  tasks:

  - name: Run the fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql script for all databases in a Postgres cluster
    sql: >
      SET SEARCH_PATH TO pg_catalog;
      RUN SELECT 'SET SCHEMA ''' || schemaname || ''';';  -- Set the correct schema for psql and SQL shell commands.
      \i /usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql; 

  - name: Check if it is template0 database
    sql: select current_database()
     register: result

  - name: Temporarily enable connections to change template0
    when: "'template0' == '{{result.stdout}}'"
    sql:
      query="ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;"

  - name: Fix template0
    when: "'template0' == '{{result.stdout}}'"
    retries: 3
    delay: 10
    sql:
       query: 'SET SCHEMA ''pg_catalog'';'
     \i /usr/share/postgresql/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql

  - name: Remove the temporary allow connection setting for template0 after fixing it
    when: "'template0' == '{{result.stdout}}'"
    sql:
      query="ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;"

  - name: Confirm the fix is performed 
    become_method: su
    when: "'template1' == '{{result.stdout}}'" or "'template0' == '{{result.stdout}}'"
    changed_when: False
    sql: select *
           from pg_class,
                pg_depend,
                pg_attribute
       where   pg_depend.refclassid  = 'pg_catalog.pg_class'::regclass
               and     pg_depend.refobjid = pg_class.oid
               and     pg_depend.deptype  = 'a'
               and     (pg_class.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
                         or pg_class.relname  = 'stats_ext')
       union
      SELECT *
        FROM (VALUE, ATTRNAME) AS V,
             pg_largeobject as p, 
                pg_largeobject_metadata as pmd
       WHERE islocal IS TRUE
               and     objid  = p.oid
               and not EXISTS  (
                    SELECT  1
                      FROM    pg_stats
                      WHERE   attrname      = V.ATTRNAME
                             AND      schemaname = 'public'
                         ) 
       -- select V.VALUE, pmd.objid
       
@@@END_FILE@@@

    - name: Fix PostgreSQL vulnerability CVE-2024-4317
      hosts: postgresql_servers
      become: yes

      tasks:
        - name: Ensure directory exists for fix script
          file:
            path: /usr/share/postgresql/{{ ansible_pg_version|int }}/
            state: directory

        - name: Copy fix-script to appropriate location if missing
          get_url:
            url: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/{{ ansible_pg_version|int }}/static/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql
            dest: /usr/share/postgresql/{{ ansible_pg_version|int }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql
          when: stat('/usr/share/postgresql/{{ ansible_pg_version|int }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql')|stat('size') != 8586 or ansible_pg_version in [14, 15, 16]

        - name: Temporarily enable connections to template0 database
          postgresql_db:
            db: template0
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            state: present
            query: ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;

        - name: Run fix script on each database (excluding template1)
          postgresql_query:
            db: "{{ item }}"
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            query: "\i /usr/share/postgresql/{{ ansible_pg_version|int }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql"
          loop: "{{ postgresql_databases | difference(['template0', 'template1']) }}"

        - name: Run fix script on template1 database (due to a bug template1 requires manual enable)
          postgresql_query:
            db: template1
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            query: "\i /usr/share/postgresql/{{ ansible_pg_version|int }}/fix-CVE-2024-4317.sql"

        - name: Disable connections to template0 database
          postgresql_db:
            db: template0
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            state: present
            query: ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;

        - name: Ensure both template databases are up to date (as this vulnerability affects database creation)
          postgresql_db:
            db: template0
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            state: present
            query: ALTER DATABASE template0 RELOAD;
          tags: [postgresql_template]

        - name: Ensure both template databases are up to date (as this vulnerability affects database creation)
          postgresql_db:
            db: template1
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            state: present
            query: ALTER DATABASE template1 RELOAD;
          tags: [postgresql_template]

      handlers:
        - name: Handle errors during connection setup/teardown
          failed_when: "{{ lookup('env', 'ANSIBLE_FAILURE_CALLBACK')|bool }}"
          ignore_errors: true
          postgresql_db:
            db: template0
            host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
            user: postgres
            password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            state: present
            query: ALTER DATABASE template0 WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
          when: ansible_failed_revdeploy
        - name: Re-run fix script if the error was caused by a different connection attempt. Ansible can replay the same tasks multiple times.
          include_task:_module_run_again_onerror
          vars:
            module_name: postgresql_query
            modules_args:
              db: template0
              host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
              user: postgres
              password: "{{ postgres_password }}"
            error_patterns:
            - ^AnsibleTaskException:\ Unreachable: FATAL: all hosts have already failed -- any remaining tasks will not be retried
            - ^Connection reset by peer
            - ^fatal:***
          when: ansible_failed[0].msg matches ('The connection to the server "{{ inventory_hostname }}" was declined because it violates the server's policy ([auth/reject_hostwith]...)' or ansible_command[0].success is false)
    @@@END_FILE@@@

fields.content:
Based on the data provided, here's a summary of the roles and permissions for each user in the system:

1. Administrators (users starting with "qa"): These users have maintenance permission across all projects (Web development, App Development, Integration, Reporting, Financials, and Metrics). This means they can modify and manage the codebases of these respective projects.

2. Developers (users without "qa" prefix): They have various roles within teams:
   - Developers working on Web development or App Development projects (user names without specific project mentioned) have maintenance permission in their assigned project(s) as well as Developer permissions for the Integration project. This allows them to modify and manage codebases for their respective projects and contribute to the Integration project.
   - Developers working only on the Financials or Metrics project (users with "Finanzen" or "Metriken" prefix) have Developer permission in those assigned projects and Reporter permissions for the Integration project, meaning they can modify codebases in their assigned projects and report findings to the Integration team.
   - Developers working solely on the Integration project (user "dev0XX" where X is a number from 1-9) have Developer permissions, which allows them to contribute to the Integration project's codebase.

3. Testers: These users don't appear in the provided data, but they are likely responsible for ensuring the quality of the software by verifying that it adheres to specified requirements and identifying defects before release.

4. External users (users with "ext001"): They have Guest access to all projects except Web development and App Development, where they only have Guest access. In these projects, external users are likely limited to viewing or testing pre-release versions, as they don't have any permission related to modifying or managing the codebases.

5.Bot accounts (users with "bot0XX" where X is a number from 1-7): They each have Maintainer permissions across different projects. Most likely, these accounts are used by automated tools for CI/CD (Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment) pipelines to perform actions on behalf of the team like building, testing, and updating codebases.

6. Infrastructure team: These users have ownership of the infrastructure that supports development and deployment activities for all projects in the system. They are not developers but are responsible for ensure the correct functioning of tools, servers, networks, and other systems that team members depend on.
